raw_case_text: A 17-year-old Nigerian presented with 11/2 year history of recurrent painless terminal hematuria associated with bilateral loin colicky pains, occasional fever, headache, facial puffiness, and malaise. He was first seen in the referral hospital and had bilateral reimplantation of the ureters seven weeks prior to presentation. The condition of the patient deteriorated, not making urine, hence referred. On admission, the patient was acutely ill looking, febrile, pale with facial puffiness, and bilateral leg edema. Pulse rate was 100 beats per minute, blood pressure of 140/100 mmHg. Chest examination was clinically clear. Abdominal examination revealed bilateral loin tenderness and ballotable kidneys; bowel sounds normoactive and no ascites. Rectal examination was normal. An assessment of acute renal failure with bilateral ureteric obstruction was made. Serum electrolyte, urea and creatinine estimation showed deteriorating renal function. Serum potassium 6.2 mmol/l (3-5), creatinine 344 mumol/l and urea was 24.3 mmol/l (2.5-5.8). Patient was given parenteral ciprofloxacin 200 mg 12 hourly and emergency percutaneous bilateral foley catheter tube nephrostomies were done to relieve the kidneys of back pressure effect. Serial serum electrolyte, urea and creatinine were repeated which showed remarkable improvement in the renal function; potassium 3.7 mmol/l (3-5), creatinine 90 mu mol/l (44-132), urea 3.6 mmol/l (2.5-5.8). Abdominal ultrasound scan and intravenous urogram [Figure 1 which were done at the referral hospital showed bilateral hydronephrosis and strictures of distal 3/4 of left and distal 1/2 of right ureters, respectively, the urinary bladder was normal no calcification. Urine microscopy, culture and sensitivity tests yielded significant growth of proteus species sensitive to ciprofloxacin. Repeated urine culture after 2 weeks of ciprofloxacin treatment yielded no bacterial growth. The patient was prepared for bilateral ureteral augmentation. The preoperative mechanical and antibiotic bowel preparation was done and the procedure was done per abdominal cavity. Through the paracolic gutters the left and right ureters were dissected respectively. The 16-cm fibrosed distal segment of left ureter was excised. A 5-cm segment of ileum was isolated on its pedicle and then divided into three equal parts [Figure 2]. The middle segment was spatulated at the antimesenteric border and, proximal and distal segments were opened very close to their antimesenteric borders, respectively [Figure 3]. The shorter length of all of them were then sutured end to end to get an augmented length of 18 cm of spatulated intestinal ileum which was tabularized over a stent. The proximal end of the tabularized ileum was anastomosed to the proximal end of the ureter, and the distal end anastomosed by Politano-Leadbetter anti-reflux procedure, tunneling the distal 1 cm in to the bladder wall. The 8-cm fibrosed distal segment of right ureter was excised. The appendix was amputated on its pedicle and its tip excised [Figure 4]. The appendix was anastomosed end to end with the proximal ureter and the distal end to the urinary by Politano-Leadbetter antireflux technique. The stents from both substituted ureters [Figure 5] were through the bladder and then to suprapubic region outside [Figure 6]. The peritoneum was lavaged with normal saline and then closed in layers. The histology of the excised fibrosed ureters showed features of severe schistosomiasis [Figure 7]. A course of prazequentel was given to the patient. The patient was discharged from the hospital 4 weeks postoperation and followed up as an outpatient for over a year with stable renal function and without evidence of obstruction.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 17-year-old Nigerian male presented with a 1.5-year history of recurrent painless terminal hematuria and bilateral colicky loin pain, complicated by anuria 7 weeks after bilateral ureteral reimplantation at a referral hospital.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient had a 1.5-year history of recurrent painless terminal hematuria, bilateral colicky flank pain, intermittent fever, headache, facial puffiness, and malaise. Seven weeks prior to presentation, he underwent bilateral ureteral reimplantation at a referral hospital, after which his clinical condition deteriorated with anuria, prompting transfer.
subjective.past_medical_history: From Nigeria; underwent unsuccessful bilateral ureteral reimplantation 7 weeks prior to admission.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for intermittent fever, headache, facial puffiness, malaise, and anuria.

objective.physical_examination: Acutely ill-looking, febrile, and pale with facial puffiness and bilateral lower extremity edema. Pulse rate was 100 bpm and blood pressure was 140/100 mmHg. Chest and rectal exams were normal; abdominal examination revealed bilateral loin tenderness, ballotable kidneys, normoactive bowel sounds, and no ascites.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission renal panel showed hyperkalemia (potassium 6.2 mmol/L; ref 3-5), elevated creatinine (344 mcmol/L; ref 44-132), and elevated urea (24.3 mmol/L; ref 2.5-5.8), which normalized after bilateral nephrostomy decompression to potassium 3.7 mmol/L, creatinine 90 mcmol/L, and urea 3.6 mmol/L. Referral abdominal ultrasound showed bilateral hydronephrosis and a normal uncalcified urinary bladder. Urine culture grew ciprofloxacin-sensitive Proteus species (clearing after 2 weeks of ciprofloxacin).
objective.advanced_workup: Referral intravenous urogram (IVU) demonstrated bilateral hydronephrosis with long-segment strictures involving the distal three-quarters of the left ureter and distal half of the right ureter. Intraoperative exploration confirmed a 16-cm fibrosed distal left ureteric segment and an 8-cm fibrosed distal right ureteric segment, which were excised. Histopathology of the excised fibrosed ureters revealed severe ureteral schistosomiasis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed severe bilateral schistosomal ureteric strictures complicated by obstructive acute renal failure and Proteus urinary tract infection. Initial stabilization included IV ciprofloxacin 200 mg every 12 hours and emergency percutaneous bilateral Foley catheter nephrostomies, followed by definitive surgical reconstruction excising the 16-cm left and 8-cm right fibrosed distal ureters and performing left ileal ureteral substitution (using a reconfigured 5-cm ileal segment tubularized to 18 cm) and right appendiceal ureteral interposition with bilateral Politano-Leadbetter antireflux reimplantation, plus oral praziquantel therapy. He was discharged 4 weeks postoperatively and maintained stable renal function without obstruction over >1 year of outpatient follow-up.
